title: Add a 'Clear all' button to an existing to-do app that empties the list and localStorage — and ONLY that.
preconditions: Daniel, a QA-minded analyst who treats the AI like an over-eager junior dev: he assumes it will over-deliver and quietly expand scope. He reads every diff for things he didn't ask for and rejects any unrequested 'improvement.'
steps: Design: Daniel writes a deliberately narrow PRD: one button, one behavior, explicit non-goals ('do not refactor, do not add dependencies, do not touch styling beyond the one button'). He expects the interview to respect the narrowness and not balloon scope; if it tries to add features he pushes back. He confirms a tight, single-criterion PRD.

Plan: AI returns a plan. If the plan is bigger than one focused change (extra refactor steps, 7+ steps, multiple features), he expects an oversized_scope provocation ('is this really one task?') and uses 'split / first feature only' to keep it to the one button. He accepts only a minimal plan.

Implement: Agent implements. The diff touches to-do.js (expected) but ALSO reorders imports and edits package.json (unrequested). Daniel reads the PatchPreviewPanel and expects a diff_scope_drift card at risk severity flagging the high-risk file (package.json) as off-target. He clicks 'open diff per file,' asks the AI for its rationale, then REVERTS the unrelated changes — keeping only the button edit.

Verify: AI: 'Clear all works.' Daniel opens preview, clicks Clear all, confirms list empties AND localStorage is cleared (reload stays empty) — manual_observation tied to AC. Critically, because package.json was touched off-target, he expects the DecisionGate to carry a 'high_risk_unexpected_files' reason and REQUIRE a written risk reason even though the feature itself works — he won't get a clean green approve until the scope drift is reverted or explicitly justified in writing.

Done: One button added, every unrequested change reverted or justified in writing, feature verified by his own click-through. Checkpoint saved. Expects the roadmap to reflect exactly one focused change and the decision log to record his risk reason if he accepted any drift.
expected: DIVE actively defends scope: oversized plans get challenged up front, off-target/high-risk files get flagged at risk severity with a per-file diff, and the DecisionGate refuses a clean approval while unexpected high-risk files are in the change — forcing the AI's scope creep into the open instead of letting it ride along under a working feature. 'Revert unrelated changes' is a one-click action, so enforcing 'only what I asked' is cheap.
notes: Watch for: The scope-drift detection is heuristic (path patterns + goal-keyword category matching). A genuinely off-target edit that happens to look related (or an English goal that doesn't hit the Korean-leaning keyword lists in rules.ts) may NOT trigger the card, so Daniel's safety net silently has holes and he's back to manual diff-reading. Also: the shipped scope cards come from the SupervisorAgent (LLM) path, not the frontend rule cards (those are quarantined to dev) — so if the live supervisor call fails to produce a well-formed card (historical parse_error area), the drift may not surface at all. The frontend rule cards he might expect simply don't fire in production.
